name: Centro Historico (Plaza Grande)
description: The area around Plaza Vasco de Quiroga is Patzcuaro's grandest space, lined with arcaded colonial buildings, artisan shops, and the Basilica de Nuestra Senora de la Salud just uphill. It's the most polished and tourist-frequented part of town, with the best mix of cafes, boutique hotels, and easy walking access to everything else.
bestFor: First-time visitors and short-term stays wanting everything walkable
cons: Busiest with tourists and festival crowds

name: Plaza Chica (Gertrudis Bocanegra)
description: A few blocks from Plaza Grande, Plaza Chica is where daily local life actually happens, anchored by the sprawling mercado municipal, cheap fondas, and the public library housed in a former church. It feels less staged than Plaza Grande and is a great base for anyone wanting proximity to markets and authentic street food.
bestFor: Budget-conscious nomads who want to live like a local
pros: Cheapest food and produce in town
cons: Noisier and more chaotic than Plaza Grande

name: Lakefront / Muelle General
tagline: Where the town meets Lake Patzcuaro
description: Down the hill from the historic center, the lakefront and public pier area is the departure point for boats to Janitzio island and a quieter, more residential stretch of town. It has a working-harbor feel with fish stalls and boat operators rather than boutique charm, and offers the closest access to the lake itself.
bestFor: Nature lovers wanting easy lake and boat access
pros: Direct access to Janitzio boat trips
cons: 10 to 15 minute walk or short ride to the main plazas

name: Tzintzuntzan (nearby lake village)
tagline: An ancient Purepecha capital on the lakeshore
description: About 20 minutes by combi from Patzcuaro, Tzintzuntzan was once the capital of the Purepecha empire and retains striking pyramid ruins overlooking the lake alongside a low-key artisan pottery village. It's less a base for daily nomad life than a nearby escape and a window into pre-Hispanic Michoacan history.
bestFor: Day trips and travelers wanting a slower, more rural lakeside setting
pros: Cheaper and quieter than Patzcuaro proper
cons: Limited services and no real coworking options
Requires a short commute into Patzcuaro for amenities
